title: Sell Mineral Rights in Movico, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Movico, AL | Mobile County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Movico, AL north of Mobile? Get a straightforward, courthouse-researched offer with no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Movico sits in the industrial corridor north of Mobile, where rail and river infrastructure built up around Chickasaw and Prichard shaped how much of the surrounding land got sold, subdivided, and eventually built on.
intro: Industrial development along this stretch of Mobile County has a way of obscuring what's underneath a piece of land — a family that sold a parcel to a rail or shipping concern decades ago may still hold the mineral rights, since industrial buyers were often interested in the surface for facilities and right-of-way, not in what might be produced below it. If your family has ties to Movico or the surrounding area, that's the first thing worth checking before assuming any old mineral interest is gone.

sections.heading: Industrial Surface Sales That Left Minerals Behind
paragraphs: Rail and shipping companies buying land in this corridor a generation or two ago frequently didn't bother acquiring the mineral estate, since it had no bearing on their use of the surface. We check whether that's the case for any Movico-area tract your family has a connection to, rather than assuming a sale decades ago covered everything.

sections.heading: What's Actually on Record
paragraphs: Because this area has changed hands industrially as much as it has residentially, the Mobile County Probate Court record is the most reliable way to confirm what your family still owns. We pull that record ourselves before quoting a number, since assumptions based on what the land looks like today rarely match what the deed actually says.

faqs.question: Our family sold land near Movico to a rail or shipping company years ago. Could we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: It's possible — industrial buyers often didn't acquire mineral rights along with the surface. We check the specific deed to find out.

faqs.question: The land looks completely industrial now. Does that mean the mineral rights are worthless?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Surface use doesn't determine mineral value on its own — we look at whether the tract has ever been leased or sits near active production.

faqs.question: How do we start if we're not even sure we still own anything?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever you have — an old deed, a family name, even a rough location — and we'll check the Mobile County record from there.

faqs.question: Would a small mineral fraction near Movico even be worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Small fractions in this corridor still carry real value if the underlying tract has ever been leased, so it's worth confirming rather than assuming.
